dress_code.men: Traditional dhotis, panchas, kurtas, or standard formal trousers with shirts are standard. For special rituals like Rudrabhishekam puja, men must wear a white dhoti and remove their upper shirt and vest.
dress_code.women: Traditional attire like sarees, salwar suits, salwar kameez, chudidhars with a dupatta, or half-sarees are strongly recommended. Avoid short skirts, sleeveless kurtis, or revealing dresses (avoid western casuals like shorts or ripped jeans).

dos: Dress traditionally: Wear modest clothing like sarees or salwar suits for women, and dhotis or formal trousers for men.
Remove shirts for sevas: Men must remove their upper shirt and vest if participating in the Rudrabhishekam puja.
Secure belongings: Keep bags and personal items clutched tightly to protect them from aggressive local monkeys.
Visit on weekdays: Schedule your darshan between Tuesday and Thursday morning to avoid long weekend queue lines.
Follow queue lines: Stay within the designated barricades and respect the instructions of the temple security guards.
donts: No photography: Do not take photos or videos inside the main sanctum, as cameras are strictly prohibited.
Avoid western casuals: Do not wear short skirts, sleeveless tops, shorts, or ripped jeans inside the temple premises.
No open food: Do not carry exposed food items or plastics openly, as they attract monkey attacks.
Avoid festival rushes: Senior citizens should avoid visiting during Sharad Navaratri due to exhausting outdoor waiting times.
No footwear inside: Do not enter the inner temple courtyard with shoes or sandals; leave them at the designated footwear stand outside.
electronic_ban: Cameras and photography/videography are strictly prohibited inside the main sanctum. Safe cloakrooms and lockers are available near entrance counters to deposit bags, footwear, and mobile devices.
safety_guidelines: Keep bags and personal items clutched tightly to protect them from aggressive local monkeys. Do not carry exposed food items or plastics openly as they attract monkey attacks.
